questions.text:
Write at least 400 words in te reo Māori on ONE of the following topics. Use the planning space to map out your ideas. A list of words is provided after three of the topics to help with ideas — you do not have to use them.

Topic 1: He ao rerekē tēnei e noho nei tātou ki tērā o ngā whakatupuranga o mua. He nui rawa atu ngā mea pēnei i te hangarau o te wā e whakaaware ana i ngā taiohi. Heoi anō, he nui anō ngā angitutanga e āhei ai ngā taiohi ki te eke ki ngā taumata o tēnei ao.
Kia pōhewa ai koe kua eke koe ki te 40 tau. Tuhia he reta ki a koe anō ki tō pakeke o naiānei e āta whakamārama kia pēhea tō eke ki te angitū o tēnei ao hurihuri.
The world we are living in is different to that of previous generations. There are many distracting things but also many opportunities. Imagine you are now 40 years old. Write a letter to yourself at your current age explaining how to succeed in this changing world.
Kuputaka: Angitu(-tanga) = success/opportunity; Mātauranga = education; Te taha hinengaro = the mental side; Te taha tinana = the physical side; Te taha wairua = the spiritual side; Te taha whānau = the social side; Umanga = career; Whakapau kaha = invest energy into something

Topic 2: He kairīpoata koe mō te niupepa reo Māori e kīia nei ko 'Te Karere o Aotearoa'. Kua tae koe ki te wāhi e tū ana tētahi kaupapa hītori whakahirahira. Ko tāu mahi he tuhi mō taua kaupapa hei whakamōhio atu ki ngā kaipānui.
You are a reporter for the Māori language newspaper 'Te Karere o Aotearoa'. You have arrived at a place that an important historical event is happening. Write an article about the important aspects of that event.
Consider events such as the battle of Ōrākau, Te Petihana Reo Māori, the protest for the seabed and foreshore, Māui catching the sun, the arrival of Kupe to Aotearoa etc.
Kuputaka: Hua = outcome; Kare ā-roto = emotions/feelings; Oranga tonutanga = survival/continued wellbeing; Pānga = affect; Pā(-ngia) = effect; Tohe = argue; Tutuki = to achieve; Wawata = dream; Whāinga = goal; Whakamātau = to try

Topic 3: He reo motuhake te reo Māori. Ko te reo tūturu o tēnei whenua. Heoi anō, ka tata ngaro te reo pērā i te moa i ngā tau kua hipa. I ahatia te reo? Kei te pēhea te oranga o te reo i ēnei rā? Ki tō whakaaro, me aha tātou hei whakarauora i te reo i ngā tau kei te heke mai?
Te Reo Māori is a unique language. It is the original language of this country. However, it nearly disappeared. What happened to the language? What is the state of the language now? What do we need to do to revitalise the language in the years to come?
Write an essay with an introduction, body, and conclusion.
Kuputaka: Heke = decline; Kura taketake = Native school; Mīmiti/tāharahara = diminish; Pēhi(-a)/tāmi(-a) = oppress; Pūnaha = system; Rautaki = strategy; Taiwhenua = rural; Ture = law; Tutuki = achieve; Whakapākehā(-tia) = assimilate into a European lifestyle; Whakarauora(-ngia) = revive; Whakatāonetanga = urbanisation

Topic 4: I mua i te taenga mai o te Pākehā ki Aotearoa, kāore he pukapuka. Ka heke mai ngā pūrākau me ngā pakiwaitara mai i tētahi whakatupuranga ki tētahi atu, mai i te waha o te kaikōrero ki ngā taringa o te kaiwhakarongo. Ka puritia ēnei kōrero tuku iho ki te whatumanawa o te tangata. Ka whakaohooho ēnei kōrero i a tātou. Ko tāu mahi hei whakarite i tō ake whakaari, pakiwaitara, pūrākau rānei hei whakaohooho i te kaipānui.
Before the arrival of Pākehā to Aotearoa, there were no books. The stories were passed down from generation to generation. These stories inspire us. Write your own play, story, or pūrākau to inspire the reader.
No helping words are provided for this topic.
questions.markingGuide:
This is a writing exam where you choose ONE topic and write at least 400 words in te reo Māori only. Use the planning space to brainstorm your answer.

Achieved (Paetae 3-4): Candidate writes in te reo Māori about topics from a local, national, or global perspective. Uses phrases and language features that are relevant to the topic. Expresses ideas and opinions. Produces a piece of writing that is mostly understood despite errors. Attempts to use basic writing conventions. Uses a basic range of relevant vocabulary, grammar, and language features in te reo Māori.

Merit (Kaiaka 5-6): Candidate writes in te reo Māori with substance about topics from a local, national, or global perspective. Develops ideas, opinions, or perspectives in a logical sequence. Connects main ideas with examples, explanations, and conclusions. Produces a piece of writing that is understood despite minor errors. Demonstrates an understanding of writing conventions. Consistently utilises a range of appropriate grammar and language features in te reo Māori. For KA6: writing is clearly understood with good grammar and sentence structure; may have used more features of the language.

Excellence (Kairangi 7-8): Candidate writes in te reo Māori with purpose/clear intent about topics from a local, national, or global perspective. Integrates evidence fluently and purposefully. Carefully constructs their written answer by enhancing, supporting with evidence, and reinforcing their thinking. Produces an in-depth piece of writing that is easily understood. Well-structured and coherent, following a logical sequence of thought. Demonstrates a comprehensive understanding of writing conventions. Consistently utilises a wide range of appropriate grammar and language features in te reo Māori. For KR8: writing has minimal errors and uses higher-level grammar, structures, and other features of the language.
